newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest buyout approved, offering seen.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest buyout approved, offering seen.

text.p: TimberWest Forest Ltd shareholders on Wednesday approved a C$674 million takeover deal for the lumber company by a 98.5 percent margin.
The company is being bought for C$22 a share by a group of institutional investors who are turning it into an income trust.
A representative of the acquiring group told reporters after Wednesday's meeting that a public offering of trust units is planned.

The buyout is expected to close in the third week of June. Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd, which owns 52 percent of TimberWest, will receive C$348 million for its shares. TimberWest will also refinance C$240 million in debt owed to Fletcher at the closing of the deal.

Fletcher precipitated an auction for TimberWest last autumn, saying its stake in the lumber company did not fit with its desire to focus on its paper business. After a search for buyers failed to yield a satisfactory offer, TimberWest announced a plan to turn itself into an income trust.
That effort was aborted in March when brokerage Goepel Shields proposed an income trust on behalf of 15 institutions.
They are financing the deal partly by selling TimberWest's three sawmills and timber rights in the interior of British Columbia to Slocan Forest Products Ltd for C$200 million.
Despite speculation in March that some shareholders were unhappy with the C$22 a share price, not a single objection to the deal was raised at Wednesday's meeting.

Doug Whitehead, TimberWest chairman and president of Fletcher Canada, said this reflected general support for the acquisition and the view that C$22 was "a good, fair price." TimberWest was wholly owned by Fletcher Canada until 1993 when it went public at C$13 a share.
Don Shumka, a Goepel Shields executive who is overseeing the acquisition, said his firm plans to launch a small public issue of trust units "almost immediately" after the closing.
This would involve Goepel's own stake in the deal which he said was about C$8 million. "Our objective is to have a publicly traded security as soon as possible," Shumka said.
Then before the end of the year, the institutions plan to offer a roughly 25 percent stake in TimberWest to replace about C$160 million in bridge financing.

He declined to comment on the potential price of the offering and said the pricing would be geared to interest rates rather than stock market trends. This is because income trusts are oriented around cash flow and yield.
The institutions, which include major Canadian pension and mutual funds, plan to run the company along the same lines as its prior management, leaving key executives in place.

Despite previous speculation to the contrary, Shumka said no sale of TimberWest's privately owned timberlands was planned. In fact, he said acquisition of more timberland might ultimately be considered, although this would likely have to occur outside British Columbia where there are few parcels of private forest left.
Closing of the deal is contingent on provincial government approval which Shumka said was possible by the end of May.
